rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God abundantly conceals the innumerable past sins of those who sinned against Him despite His beneficence to them.
rows.anchor: المحسن إلينا مع إساءتنا {لغفور} للمذنبين فيبالغ في ستر ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exceedingly rewarding to the obedient; divine gratitude means recompense, reward, and requital.
rows.anchor: {شكور} للمطيعين فيبالغ في إثابتهم فإن الشكر من الله الإثابة والجزاء والوفاق.

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat reads Ghafur for the self-wronging and Shakur for the moderate and foremost; the sinner is named first gently because their state is weak.
rows.anchor: غفور للظالم لنفسه شكور للمقتصد والسابق وإنما قدم ما للظالم رفقا بهم لضعف أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saved inhabitants describe God with a further attribute of gratitude as they praise Him.
rows.anchor: ثم وصفوا الله بوصف آخر هو شكر له فقالوا :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥallanā means He settled or brought us down; ḥalla first described unloading baggage on arrival, then came to mean lodging generally.
rows.anchor: أنزلنا يقال حلت نزلت من حل الأحمال عند النزول ثم جرد استعماله للنزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dar al-muqāmah is the second object of aḥalla, not an adverb, because it denotes a bounded place.
rows.anchor: {دار المقامة} مفعول ثان لأحل وليست بظرف لأنها محدودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ḍamma, muqāmah is a verbal noun of residence: the everlasting home from which no one departs or wishes to depart.
rows.anchor: والمقامة بالضم مصدر تقول أقام يقيم إقامة ومقامة أي : دار الإقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is bestowed from God's favor without any deed obligating Him; even good works are themselves His favor.
rows.anchor: من أنعامه وتفضله من غير أن يوجبه شيء من قبلنا من الأعمال فإن الحسنات فضل منه أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entry into Paradise is by grace and mercy, while ranks are apportioned by deeds; since deeds are created, they earn no compensation from their Master, contrary to Mu'tazilite claims that God owes it.
rows.anchor: فكيف الظن بمن له الملك على الإطلاق أيستحق من يعبده عوضا عن عبادته تعالى الله عما يقول المعتزلة من الإيجاب

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat says the wrongdoer, moderate, and foremost each enters a station God assigned by grace, not by personal effort or deeds.
rows.anchor: دخل كل واحد من الظالم والمقتصد والسابق في مقام أحله الله فيه من فضله لا بجهده وعمله

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Even when Paradise is given as recompense for deeds, God's prior enabling of the good deed is already a favor.
rows.anchor: وأن الذي أدخله الله الجنة جزاء بعمله فتوفيقه للعمل الصالح أيضا من فضل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying illustrates grace without a causal claim: acceptance is not due to an independent cause, nor rejection to one.
rows.anchor: قبل من قبل لا لعلة ورد من رد لا لعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden has no bodily toil or pain of the kind experienced in worldly life.
rows.anchor: {لا يمسنا} المس كاللمس وقد يقال في كل ما ينال الإنسان من أذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghūb is fatigue and slackness; it is absent because the Garden has no religious burden or toil.
rows.anchor: كلال وفتور إذ لا تكليف فيها ولا كد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in the Garden see God without travelling or waiting, and without directing or straining their eyes toward a direction; the vision has no describable modality.
rows.anchor: وإذا أرادوا أن يروه لا يحتاجون إلى قطع مسافة وانتظار وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣab is the hardship itself; laghūb is the bodily slackness that results from it.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين النصب واللغوب أن النصب نفس المشقة والكلفة واللغوب ما يحدث منه من الفتور للجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are those who deny God's existence or His oneness.
rows.anchor: جحدوا بوجود الله تعالى أو بوحدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hellfire is the recompense for their disbelief, the greatest of sins and ugliest of acts, and is unlike ordinary fire.
rows.anchor: بمقابلة كفرهم الذي هو أكبر الكبائر وأقبح القبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not sentenced to a second death that would let them escape and rest from torment.
rows.anchor: لا يحكم عليهم بموت ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fayamutū is subjunctive through an implicit an because it answers a negation.
rows.anchor: ونصبه بإضمار ان لأنه جواب النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is not lightened for even an instant; whenever the fire subsides, its blazing is increased.
rows.anchor: طرفه عين بل كلما خبت زيد استعارها يعني : (هركاه كه آتش فرونشيند زياده كنند احراق والتهاب اورا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kashf al-asrar explains that the fire's temporary diminution is not a lessening of their punishment, since it is then increased again.
rows.anchor: قوله كلما خبت لا يدل على تخفيف عنهم بل على نقصان في النار ثم يزداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax permits ʿanhum to be the نائب الفاعل with min ʿadhābihā in the accusative, or the reverse; if min is redundant, the latter must be nominative.
rows.anchor: قوله عنهم نائب مناب الفاعل ومن عذابها في موقع النصب أو بالعكس وإن كانت زائدة يتعين له الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the pattern of such a dreadful punishment: no lighter or lesser recompense is given to every intense disbeliever or ingrate.
rows.anchor: أي : مثل هذا الجزاء الفظيع

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some define a mosque's neighbor as someone living within forty homes in every direction; another view is whoever hears the call to prayer.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : جار المسجد أربعون دارا من كل جانب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If two mosques are nearby, choose the older because it has greater sanctity; if equal, choose the nearer. A scholar may choose the one with fewer attendees to increase its congregation; others may choose freely.
rows.anchor: رجل لو كان في جواره مسجدان يصلي في أقدمهما لأن له زيادة حرمة وإن كانا سواء أيهما أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For congregational acts such as obligatory prayers and tarawih, praying in a mosque is better; a home congregation earns less reward than a mosque congregation.
rows.anchor: كل ما فيه الجماعة كالفرائض والتراويح فالمسجد فيه أفضل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says congregational prayer yields twenty-five times the reward of prayer at home or in the market; another version says twenty-seven, matching seventeen obligatory and ten regular prayers.
rows.anchor: صلاة الرجل في جماعة تضعف على صلاته في بيته

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars hold that congregational prayer is obligatory.
rows.anchor: وأكثر العلماء على أن الجماعة واجبة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some scholars instead call congregational prayer a confirmed sunnah.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : سنة مؤكدة وفي الحديث :

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said he considered ordering someone else to lead prayer and burning the homes of those who stayed away; the author argues he would not intend a sinful act, so this supports the permissibility of burning a home for abandoning an obligation or confirmed sunnah.
rows.anchor: لقد هممت أن آمر رجلا يصلي بالناس وأنظر إلى أقوام يتخلفون عن الجماعة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises complete light on Judgment Day to those who walk to mosques in darkness; the author says only severe darkness can excuse absence, alongside other manifest excuses.
rows.anchor: بشروا المشائين في الظلم إلى المساجد بالنور التام يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excuses for missing congregational prayer include illness warranting tayammum, disabling injury or paralysis, inability to walk, blindness, rain, mud, severe cold or darkness, and fear of rulers or other oppressors.
rows.anchor: والأعذار التي تبيح التخلف عن الجماعة هي المرض الذي يبيح التيمم ومثله كونه مقطوع اليد والرجل من خلاف أو مفلوجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull shayʾ means absolutely everything, whether made by a human being or by someone else.
rows.anchor: من الأشياء كائنا ما كان سواء كان ما يصنعه الإنسان أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull shayʾ is governed by an implicit verb explained by aḥṣaynāhu, meaning that God recorded, bounded, and made it clear.
rows.anchor: وهو منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره قوله :

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says iḥṣāʾ originally means counting, then by metaphor came to mean clarification and preservation, since counting serves those ends.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : أصل الإحصاء العد ثم استعير للبيان والحفظ

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines iḥṣāʾ as collecting by number; its name derives from pebbles, once used for counting as fingers are now.
rows.anchor: الإحصاء التحصيل بالعدد يقال : أحصيت كذا وذلك من لفظ الحصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifest register is the Preserved Tablet, a great and comprehensive source manifesting everything past and future; it is called an imam because it is followed.
rows.anchor: أصل عظيم الشان مظهر لجميع الأشياء مما كان وما سيكون وهو اللوح المحفوظ سمي إماما لأنه يؤتم به ويتبع

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines imam as something followed, such as a person, book, or other guide, whether rightly or wrongly; its plural is aʾimmah.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الإمام المؤتم به إنسانا كان يقتدي بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse has also been interpreted as referring to the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: فقد قيل : إشارة إلى اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's comprehensive recording both warns and encourages: knowing nothing escapes record should make a person watch every breath, movement, and stillness.
rows.anchor: وفي الإحصاء ترغيب وترهيب فإن المحصى لم يصح منه الغفلة في حال من الأحوال بل راقب نفسه في كل وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting this divine name twenty times over each of twenty pieces of broken bread is said to subdue people's hearts.
rows.anchor: خاصية هذا الاسم تسخير القلوب فمن قرأه عشرين مرة على كل كسرة من الخبز والكسر عشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subduing people can avert harm or bring benefit, especially through teaching and guidance, but some great Sufis leave influence to God's will; mastery of the lower self matters more than outward authority.
rows.anchor: واختار بعض الكبار ترك التصرف والالتفات إلى جانب الخلق بضرب من الحيل

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya reads everything done to draw near to God as effects and lights inscribed in the Preserved Tablet of the beloveds' hearts.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" {وكل شىء}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfected human heart is a divine manifest tablet bearing lights of the unseen kingdom and imprinted mysteries of the realm of power, accessible after purification beyond ordinary human and rational capacities.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن قلب الإنسان الكامل اسم مبين ولوح إلهي فيه أنوار الملكوت منتقشة وأسرار الجبروت منطبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shining sun is an inward sign of the effusion of the light of existence onto created forms through divine manifestations.
rows.anchor: الشمس المضيئة المشرقة على صحائف الكائنات كإشراق نور الوجود مطلق الفائض على هياكل الموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the lām as purpose and mustaqarr as a place: the sun travels to a fixed destination at the end of its annual course, like a traveller reaching a stop.
rows.anchor: الأول أن اللام في المستقر للتعليل والمستقر اسم مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading makes the lām mean to and the destination the middle of the sky; the sun seems to pause there because its motion is so slow, not because it truly stops.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن اللام بمعنى إلى والمستقر كبد السماء

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat explains that zawāl normally describes something formerly stationary; noon is treated as the sun's stable position only by customary perception.
rows.anchor: في "المفردات" : الزوال يقال في شيء قد كان ثابتا

rows.speaker: شرح التقويم
rows.claim: Sharḥ al-Taqwīm says the planets are called moving because they move quickly relative to the slower fixed stars; the sun's motion is especially slow.
rows.anchor: في "شرح التقويم" : فإن قلت : لم سميت السيارة بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis treats the lām as indicating consequence and mustaqarr as a verbal noun: the sun's course produces its station in each of twelve zodiac signs for a month.
rows.anchor: والثالث أن اللام لام العاقبة والمستقر مصدر ميمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's annual course changes the relative lengths of day and night, reaches its highest summer and lowest winter points, and brings seasons and conditions for earthly livelihood and growth.
rows.anchor: بأن تستقر في كل برج شهرا ويأخذ الليل من النهار في نصف الحول والنهار من الليل في النصف الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reading takes mustaqarr as a daily endpoint, with the sun's course measured through its risings and settings; the excerpt ends while stating its 360-part circuit.
rows.anchor: والرابع أن المعنى المنتهى مقدر لكل يوم من المشارق والمغارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative al-qamara is governed by an omitted verb explained by the explicit one, as in Zaydan ḍarabtuhu; the sense is that God appointed the moon.
rows.anchor: بالنصب بإضمار فعل يفسره الظاهر كما في زيدا ضربته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon has twenty-eight stations divided among the twelve zodiac signs and passes through exactly one each night.
rows.anchor: وهي ثمان وعشرون مقسومة على الاثني عشر برجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At its final station the moon becomes thin and crescent-shaped, then is hidden for two nights in a thirty-day month or one in a twenty-nine-day month.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان في آخر منازله دق واستقوس ويستتر ليلتين إن كان الشهر ثلاثين أو ليلة إن كان تسعة وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet fasted eight or nine Ramadans; five had twenty-nine days and the remainder had thirty.
rows.anchor: وقد صام عليه السلام ثمانية أو تسعة رمضانات خمسة منها كانت تسعة وعشرين يوما والباقي ثلاثين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The authenticated report that the two festival months do not fall short means a twenty-nine-day month has the same merit as a thirty-day month.
rows.anchor: والباقي ثلاثين وقد قال عليه السلام :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muslim community follows the Arabic lunar cycle, whose reckoning is based on months rather than the solar cycle's reckoning by days.
rows.anchor: وقد صح أن دور هذه الأمة هو الدور القمري العربي الذي حسابه مبني على الشهر لا الدور الشمسي

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh locates the comparison at the end of one month and start of the next, when the moon becomes thin, curved, and yellow.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ : حتى صار القمر في آخر الشهر وأول الشهر الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUrjūn is formed from inʿirāj, crookedness; it is the date-cluster stalk between the dates and its point of attachment to the palm.
rows.anchor: فعلون من الانعراج وهو الاعوجاج وهو عود العذق ما بين شماريخه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The date cluster (ʿidhq, with kasra) corresponds to a grape cluster; the shamarīkh are the stalks bearing the unripe dates, and shamarīkh has variant plural forms.
rows.anchor: والعذق بالكسر في النخل بمنزلة العنقود في الكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aged stalks become thin, curved, and yellow; the moon resembles one in those three respects to an observer, though the moon itself is immense.
rows.anchor: فإذا قدم وعتق دق وتقوس واصفر شبه به القمر في آخر الشهر في هذه الوجوه الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadīm means old by customary usage without a fixed duration; some say it requires a year, as in the legal rule freeing a slave owned for a year under an oath.
rows.anchor: فالقديم ما تقادم عهده بحكم العادة ولا يشترط في إطلاق لفظ القديم عليه مدة بعينها

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: A Kashf al-asrar account says the moon first had complete light, looked at itself with admiration, and Gabriel struck its face and removed the light, leaving visible marks.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (ازروى حكمت كفته اندكه زيادت ونقصان ماه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited as saying the lunar marks are Gabriel's traces; the light was taken but the mark remained, bearing the testimony of divine oneness and messengership.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كفت آن خطهاكه برروى ماه مى بينيد نشان ر جبرائيل است

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: In the same account, the moon is excluded from the divine court, seeks angelic intercession, and is allowed to prostrate once monthly on the fourteenth night; its light waxes as it approaches and wanes as it recedes.
rows.anchor: ماه ازفرشتكان مدد خواست تا از بهروى شفاعت كردند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun represents a servant abiding in knowledge of God, whose illumination is constant and never eclipsed or veiled.
rows.anchor: وقيل شبيه الشمس عبد يكون ابدا في ضياء معرفته وهو صاحب تمكين غير متلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon represents a servant of changing states: expansion may raise the seeker toward union, then contraction and lapse diminish the state until God restores and refines it toward perfection.
rows.anchor: وشبيه القمر عبد تكون أحواله في التنقل وهو صاحب تلوين له من البسط ما يرقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A couplet voices the seeker's repeated descent through stations of divine love, each of which bewilders minds.
rows.anchor: ما زلت أنزل من ودادك منزلا تتحير الألباب عند نزوله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya identifies the moon with the heart, illuminated first by the spirit and then by witnessing God; its twenty-eight stations correspond to the Quran's letters.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" : وبقوله : {والقمر قدرناه منازل}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The first fourteen heart-stations are intimacy, righteousness, repentance, steadfastness, communion, forbearance, sincerity, devotion, humility, compassion, nearness, safety, yearning, and truthfulness.
rows.anchor: وهذه أسماؤها الإلفة والبر والتوبة والثبات والجمعية والحلم والخلوص والديانة والذلة والرأفة والزلفة والسلامة والشوق والصدق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The remaining heart-stations are harm, quest, thirst, love, jealousy, chivalry, proximity, generosity, gentleness, nobility, light, sainthood, guidance, and certainty.
rows.anchor: والضرر والطلب والظمأ والعشق والغيرة والفتوة والقربة والكرم واللين والمروءة والنور والولاية والهداية واليقين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: At its last station, the heart takes on Quranic character and clings to God's bond; the verse about worship until certainty marks the end of the stations of servitude.
rows.anchor: فإذا صار إلى آخر منازله فقد تخلق بخلق القرآن واعتصم بحبل الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The saying addressed to a believer in Paradise, Read and ascend, is explained as reading the Quran and rising through degrees of nearness.
rows.anchor: ويقال للمؤمن في الجنة اقرأ وارق يعني اقرأ القرآن وارتق في مقامات القرب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The heart's course begins in intimacy with God, proceeds through faith, good works, repentance, and steadfastness, and is illuminated until it becomes full; nearness to divine witnessing then erases its sense of self.
rows.anchor: فإذا ألف الحق تعالى في أول منزله ثم بر بالإيمان والعمل الصالح ثم تاب وتوجه إلى الحضرة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The heart's disappearance into God is true spiritual poverty, exemplified by the Prophet's saying, Poverty is my pride.
rows.anchor: وهذا مقام الفقر الحقيقي الذي افتخر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: On the Night Journey, the Prophet's approach to God's presence increased his poverty of being; God found him needy and enriched him by generosity.
rows.anchor: ازداد في فقره عن الوجود كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the charge that Muhammad was a poet; denying that God taught him poetry implies more forcefully that he was not a poet and the Quran is not poetry.
rows.anchor: رد وإبطال لما كانوا يقولون في حقه عليه السلام من أنه شاعر وما يقوله شعر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib traces shiʿr to fine, precise knowing and says a poet was so named for acuity and subtle knowledge; common usage later meant metered, rhymed speech.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : يقال : شعرت أصبت الشعر

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus says poetry came to denote metered verse because of its prestige, although all knowledge may be called poetry; it gives the plural ashʿār and related senses of knowing and discerning.
rows.anchor: في "القاموس" : الشعر غلب على منظوم القول لشرفه

rows.speaker: الحكماء القدماء
rows.claim: Ancient philosophers define poetry by imaginative premises, not meter or rhyme; meter and rhyme can assist imagination, and premises may combine poetic, persuasive, or demonstrative elements.
rows.anchor: والشعر عند الحكماء القدماء ليس على وزن وقافية ولا الوزن والقافية ركن في الشعر عندهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One definition distinguishes logical poetry made of false premises from conventional poetry, intentionally metered and rhymed; intention excludes accidental meter.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الشعر إما منطقي وهو المؤلف من المقدمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intentionality condition excludes Quranic phrases that happen to match poetic meters, such as the cited examples from Al Imran, Saba, and Al-Saff.
rows.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى : {لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا}

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Several Prophetic sayings happened to scan as verse without intending meter: a line after a finger was bloodied, a couplet at Hunayn or the conquest of Mecca, and lines at the trench.
rows.anchor: هل أنت إلا إصبع دميت وفي سبيل الله ما لقيت وقوله يوم حنين حين نزل ودعا واستنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetry relevant to the Quran includes logical poetry, with or without meter; logical poetry often gains currency through conventional metered verse.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشعر الواقع في القرآن الشعر المنطقي سواء كان مجردا عن الوزن أم لا والشعر المنطقي أكثر ما يروج بالاصطلاحي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says some unbelievers called the Prophet a poet because the Quran contains words with meter and rhyme.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : قال بعض الكفار للنبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: بعض المحصلين
rows.claim: Some investigators say the accusation meant that Muhammad was a liar: the Quran plainly is not structured like poetry, and poets were associated with lying, so false arguments were called poetry.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحصلين أرادوا به أنه كاذب لأن ظاهر القرآن ليس على أساليب الشعر

rows.speaker: الشريف الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Sharif al-Jurjani says people follow imaginative appeals more readily than truth when acting; poetry rests on falsehood and so is unfit for the truthful Prophet, as the saying that the best poetry is the most false suggests.
rows.anchor: قال الشريف الجرجاني في "حاشية المطالع" : والشعر وإن كان مفيدا للخواص والعوام

rows.speaker: الشريف الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani explains that God did not teach Muhammad poetry through the Quran because revelation is elevated wisdom and law, unlike contrived meter, rhyme, and weak imaginings.
rows.anchor: والمعنى وما علمنا محمدا الشعر بتعليم القرآن على معنى أن القرآن ليس بشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse signals that God taught the Prophet knowledge of former and later peoples but did not teach him Satan's poetry, which Satan called his own Quran.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية : إشارة إلى أن النبي عليه السلام معلم من عند الله

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi interprets poetry as a medium for ambiguity, riddling, and double meaning; God neither coded speech to Muhammad nor addressed him with hidden intended meanings he failed to grasp.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره الأطهر في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi asks how Ibn Arabi's reading relates to the disconnected letters at the suras' openings, and suggests he may not regard them as ambiguous or as knowledge reserved to God alone.
rows.anchor: وهل يشكل على هذه الحروف المقطعة في أوائل السور ولعله رضي الله عنه لا يرى أن ذلك من قبيل المتشابه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says all outward and inward human actions and states, including letters and crafts, occur through God's teaching.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير قوله :

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Divine teaching occurs through intermediaries, as people teach one another, or directly, as God taught David the craft of making armor.
rows.anchor: وتعليمه الصنائع لعباده على ضربين بواسطة وبغير واسطة أما بالواسطة فبتعليم بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A craft a person invents through native insight without being taught by anyone is also a form of direct divine instruction.
rows.anchor: وكل حرفة وصنعة يعملها الإنسان من قريحته بغير تعليم أحد فهي من هذا القبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi verses say the body can learn through a master of revelation, crafts originate in revelation and are developed by reason, while some skills arise without a human teacher.
rows.anchor: قابل تعليم وفهمست اين جسد ليك صاحب وحى تعليمش دهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Cain says he learned to dig a grave from a crow and then buried Abel, whom he had killed and carried for days.
rows.anchor: ثم حكى قصة قابيل فإنه تعلم حفر القبر من الغراب حتى دفن أخاه هابيل بعد قتله وحمله على عاتقه أياما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inbighāʾ derives from the root of seeking (ṭalab); bghaytuhu means I sought it, and it was attained.
rows.anchor: البغاء الطلب والإنبغاء انفعال منه يقال بغيته

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib compares ينبغي to saying fire ought to burn cloth, meaning it is made subject to burning; here poetry is neither proper nor made easy for Muhammad, even if he sought it.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : هو مثل قوله النار ينبغي أن تحرق الثوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's tongue would break the meter through inversion or similar errors, just as his inability to write or read reinforces proof of his prophethood and removes suspicion about revelation's source.
rows.anchor: لتكون الججة أثبت وشبهة المرتابين في حقية رسالته

rows.speaker: إنسان العيون
rows.claim: Insan al-ʿUyun says the prohibition is deliberately composing metered speech; accidentally metered words are not conventional poetry, and the Prophet usually disrupted meter when quoting a poem.
rows.anchor: في "إنسان العيون" والحاصل أن الحق الحقيق بالاعتماد وبه تجتمع الأقوال

rows.speaker: بعض الأدباء
rows.claim: Some literary writers claim the Prophet could intentionally compose metered verse but did not practice it, calling this more complete than inability; Bursevi says that contradicts the Quran.
rows.anchor: وادعى بعض الأدباء أنه عليه السلام كان يحسن الشعر

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi records one view that the Prophet could compose poetry but did not; the preferred view is that he could not compose it, though he could distinguish good from bad verse.
rows.anchor: للبغوي : من أئمتنا قيل كان عليه السلام يحسن الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi suggests that the Prophet's ability to distinguish good from bad poetry may mean distinguishing metered from unmetered speech.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد بين الموزون منه وغير الموزون

words: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له
rows.speaker: ينبوع الحياة
rows.claim: Yanbuʿ al-Hayah says outwardly Muslim heretics insinuated that the Prophet could compose poetry in order to undermine the Quran's denial.
rows.anchor: ثم رأيته في "ينبوع الحياة" قال : كان بعض الزنادقة المتظاهرين بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi finds that defining poetry as logical falsehood but reading what is unsuitable as metrical composition makes the two clauses of the verse fail to cohere.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشكال كما لا يخفى على ذوي الإفهام لأنهم حين حملوا الشعر في هذا الكلام على المنطقي ثم بنوا قوله وما ينبغي له على القريض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that poetry does not befit the Prophet's prophethood and truthful nature: one taught by God speaks truth. This does not deny his natural ability to compose or distinguish verse.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد وما ينبغي له من حيث نبوته وصدق لهجته أن يقول الشعر لأن المعلم من عند الله لا يقول إلا حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ability does not entail composing poetry; he refrained to avoid the label of poet and the suggestion of imaginative falsehood, though Arabs knew his eloquence, sweetness, and fine speech.
rows.anchor: لكن القدرة لا تستلزم الفعل في هذا الباب صونا عن إطلاق لفظ الشعر والشاعر الذي يوهم التخييل والكذب
